attributes.comment.frontendUrl: Set per environment by the deploy workflow to https://auth.<environment-label>.<domain>. Left empty here because a realm file with one environment's hostname baked in is a realm file that is wrong in the other two.
attributes.comment.itsm: Set by keycloak-realm.ts: the public site's home and its demo chooser. Read only by the itsm login theme's footer, and only on signed-out pages (D18). Empty means the link is not drawn.

comment.signIn: resetPasswordAllowed is false because Keycloak has no SMTP server. With it on,
'Forgot Password?' takes an address and answers 'You should receive an email
shortly' whether or not anything was sent (Keycloak 26.7 hides the failure so
the form cannot be used to find accounts), so a person waits for an email that
never comes. It goes back to true in the same change that configures SMTP.
accessCodeLifespanLogin is Keycloak's default, written down because the BFF's
pending sign-in (PENDING_TTL_SECONDS in packages/bff/src/bff.ts) is set to match
it: a login page Keycloak still accepts must not return to a BFF that has
forgotten the sign-in, or the person signs in and is told it did not finish.
The session timeouts are deliberately unchanged; raising them is a security
The theme keys (loginTheme, accountTheme, emailTheme) are deliberately absent.
Every deploy PUTs these settings, so a theme named here would be set even when
the image that carries it was never deployed. keycloak-realm.ts adds them only
when it is told the theme is running (--theme).
comment.userProfile: tenant_id is a declared user attribute, not an ad-hoc one.
apps/api/src/auth/verify.ts refuses any token whose payload has no tenant_id:
'this token names no tenant'. So the attribute, the mapper below that copies
it into the access token, and SCIM writing it at provisioning time are three
halves of one mechanism — break any and every sign-in fails closed, which is
the right direction but an expensive way to learn the claim was missing.
itsm_user_id is optional: verify.ts falls back to `sub` when it is absent.
Both are for administrators only. They are internal identifiers, so a person
reading their own account page should not be shown a tenant UUID. And a field a
person cannot see must not be required of them: Keycloak's VERIFY_PROFILE would
stop their sign-in on a form asking for a value they are not allowed to enter.
The mapper reads the attribute whatever its profile permissions say, so hiding
it changes what a person sees and not what the token carries.
comment.clientScopes: One shared scope carries the two claims the API reads, rather than four
copies of the same two mappers on four clients. A mapper that exists on
three clients out of four is the kind of fault that looks like 'only the
basic, profile and email are Keycloak's own scopes, declared here because a
realm created from a file that names any scope gets only the scopes it names.
Without them every sign-in asking for 'openid profile email' is refused as
invalid_scope, and a token without basic carries no sub.
roles, web-origins and acr are Keycloak's too, and the rest of its default
set. Our four clients do not use them; Keycloak's own account page does, and
its client (account-console) is not in this file, so keycloak-realm.ts
attaches them to it on every deploy. Without roles its API refuses every
request and the page reads 'Something went wrong'.

clientScopes.name: itsm-claims
clientScopes.description: The tenant and user claims apps/api reads off every access token

config.comment: Without this the access token's aud names the front-end client, and jwtVerify refuses it against OIDC_AUDIENCE=itsm-api. Nothing else in the token would look wrong.

clientScopes.name: basic
clientScopes.description: The subject and the authentication time. Keycloak 25 moved sub here: without this scope an access token names nobody.

clientScopes.name: profile
clientScopes.description: The person's name, which the applications show

clientScopes.name: email
clientScopes.description: The address an account is linked by on its first sign-in

clientScopes.name: roles
clientScopes.description: The account's realm and client roles. Keycloak's own account page is refused by its API without them

clientScopes.name: web-origins
clientScopes.description: The origins a browser client may call from

clientScopes.name: acr
clientScopes.description: How strongly the account was authenticated

comment.clients: Three confidential clients, one per application, and one bearer-only
resource server. Separate rather than shared because the redirect URI is
what stops an authorisation code being returned to somewhere else, and one
client holding all three origins' URIs is one compromised application away
redirectUris and webOrigins are placeholders resolved per environment by
the deploy workflow from DEPLOY_DOMAIN. The + in webOrigins means 'the
origins of the redirect URIs', so it needs no substitution.
baseUrl is resolved from the same host as the redirect URI. It is the way
back from Keycloak's error, information and logout pages, which draw 'Back to
Application' only when the client has one, and the link the account page's
name is what people see: the account page lists applications by it. It is
set from the area names by keycloak-realm.ts, so the names here are only what
that gives today. The console has a client of its own, separate from the
workbench, so that an agent session is not also a console session.

clients.name: ITSM API
clients.description: The resource server. Issues nothing; every token is addressed to it.
